text: Same acronym, two worlds. In trading card grading, PSA 10 is a gem mint card. In the clinic, a prostate-specific antigen of 10 ng/mL calls for a proper workup. I'm starting my series of short urology and biostatistics videos (in Portuguese) with this one, right in the middle of Movember. #urology #Movember #prostatecancer
Why renal colic comes in waves, and why stone size doesn't predict the pain. One minute, the way I explain it in clinic. Fever with colic is an emergency. #urology #kidneystones

Repeat the same study twenty times and p swings from 0.001 to 0.3 (Cumming, 2014, calls it the dance of the p values). One minute on what to ask instead of "was it significant?". #biostatistics #clinicalresearch
Fluid advice for stone formers is measured by urine output, not by the glass. One minute on the 2.5 L/day urine target and when to order a 24-hour urine. #urology #kidneystones
The definition of a 95% CI I use in class, with the fishing-net picture. A wide interval is not a flaw of the study; it is the data saying information is missing. #biostatistics #clinicalresearch
Many patients with calcium oxalate stones cut dairy on their own. Borghi's trial (NEJM, 2002) showed the opposite: normal calcium and low salt reduced recurrence. #urology #kidneystones
Absence of evidence is not evidence of absence (Altman and Bland, BMJ 1995). One minute on power and sample size before the first patient is enrolled. #biostatistics #clinicalresearch

Size, location and time: what weighs on the choice between waiting for a ureteral stone to pass and treating it. One minute, with the numbers from the 2007 AUA/EAU guideline (Preminger). #urology #kidneystones
The same 50% relative risk reduction can mean treating 100 patients to prevent one event, or 5. One minute on relative risk, absolute difference, NNT and odds ratio. #biostatistics #clinicalresearch
How I present kidney stone treatment options to patients: SWL, flexible ureteroscopy and PCNL, with 2 cm as the starting cut-off and the CT on the table. #endourology #urology
The thousand-people exercise, in natural frequencies as Gigerenzer proposes. The quickest way I know to show why the same test result weighs differently in each patient. #biostatistics #diagnostics
One minute for the patient who arrives worried about a raised PSA: what raises it, what to avoid before the test, and where MRI fits before biopsy. #urology #prostatecancer
The coffee-and-cigarettes example for confounding, and the limit of regression and propensity scores: they only adjust for what was measured. #biostatistics #epidemiology
Lower urinary tract symptoms in older men, explained for patients: what BPH does to the bladder and why treating it beats putting up with it. #urology #menshealth
Kaplan and Meier published the method in 1958 and it is still the first plot I look at in a survival study. One minute on steps, censoring and the log-rank test. #biostatistics #clinicalresearch
Painless gross hematuria still reaches the urologist late because the bleeding stops. One minute on why to investigate anyway: urinalysis, imaging and cystoscopy. #urology #oncology
Redelmeier (2001) and Sylvestre's reanalysis (2006) are the best example I know of immortal time bias, a frequent problem in real-world studies. #biostatistics #RWE
One minute of self-exam, once a month. Worth sending to young patients and to the sons of our patients. #urology #menshealth
The routine I give students for reading the forest plot of a meta-analysis: weights, line of no effect, diamond and heterogeneity. #metaanalysis #biostatistics
Recurrent UTI in women: definition, a urine culture for every episode, and non-antibiotic prevention before prophylaxis. One minute for patients. #urology #UTI
Borenstein and colleagues (2017) showed why I² does not measure how much the effect varies. That is why the prediction interval should sit next to the summary estimate. #metaanalysis #biostatistics
